summary: Final results are in, with Netanyahu's camp ahead but short of a majority; President Herzog says he will receive the official results on Wednesday, Nov 4, and then open consultations, and the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10. A senior Joint List official tells Walla that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot, while Netanyahu's partners are expected to back him. Ynet reports Eisenkot has had a minority government relying on Ra'am and UTJ abstentions examined, though his party says such reports don't speak for it and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties. UTJ remains the swing party, with Ynet reporting it wants draft-exemption legislation before committing to either side.

phase.now: Final results published; President Herzog says consultations begin after he receives the official results on Nov 4
phase.next: Ynet reports consultations start Nov 4 and may run into Thursday or Friday, with Herzog due to choose a candidate by Nov 11; the new Knesset is sworn in on Nov 10.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu's Right-Religious Bloc
scenarios.note: His existing partners, whom he told they are staying together. Without a majority, Netanyahu needs defectors or a new partner from the other side.

blockers.text: Liberman urged Likud MKs to revolt against Netanyahu rather than join him.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Arab Parties
scenarios.note: Championed by Yair Golan, who met Lapid and then Abbas on Oct 29; the Times of Israel says he is the only Jewish-led bloc leader openly backing a coalition with Ra'am. Without Yisrael Beiteinu it falls short, and analysts told JTA the public is not ready for it. Channel 12 reports Abbas himself privately called an Eisenkot minority government with outside Arab support weak or impossible. AFP reports Eisenkot has not decided whether to seek a coalition relying on Arab parties, and the Joint List's Jabareen says he would back him from outside. A senior Joint List official told Walla on Nov 1 that the Joint List and Ra'am are expected to recommend Eisenkot to the president.

blockers.text: Liberman ruled out Ra'am, the Joint List and any minority government.
Eisenkot pledged a 'Zionist government' and has not backed the idea.
Ben-Gvir urged the Shin Bet to arrest Arab party leaders if there are legal grounds over alleged Qatari funding.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Ra'am Only
scenarios.note: The 2021 Bennett–Lapid model. Ynet reports, citing unnamed sources, that Eisenkot authorized examining a minority government with Ra'am inside and UTJ abstaining, possibly as leverage in unity talks; Yashar says such reports are not issued on its behalf. It falls short of 61 and Liberman rejects any government dependent on Arab or Haredi parties.

scenarios.name: Change Bloc With Shas And UTJ
scenarios.note: No Arab parties needed, but the Haredi draft splits it. A source close to Eisenkot tells Ynet he is trying to bring Shas and UTJ into a government he leads, naming Liberman as the main obstacle. A senior UTJ official told Ynet the party would offer Eisenkot the premiership for draft exemptions, which clashes with his national-service condition; Shas is reported to be out.

blockers.text: Haredi sources tell the Jerusalem Post that Deri won't join an opposition-led government without Likud.
Shas and UTJ say they won't join any government unless yeshiva students' exemptions are written into law.
Liberman told party members on Oct 29 that his pledge not to sit with the Haredi parties stands.
Eisenkot's core promise is national service for all.

scenarios.name: National Unity Government
scenarios.note: The Jerusalem Post reports Netanyahu-linked sources are promoting it, possibly with a rotating premiership and without Shas and UTJ, but Ynet reports Netanyahu has not discussed it with his partners or Likud associates. Channel 12 reports Liberman wants Eisenkot to join Netanyahu, though not under his own banner. Who would lead it is the sticking point.

blockers.text: Eisenkot rules out serving under Netanyahu, including in a rotation.
Channel 12 reports Liberman still refuses to join a Netanyahu-led government, even as he urges Eisenkot to.
Ben-Gvir warned Netanyahu against a unity government with Eisenkot.

scenarios.name: Netanyahu Plus Bennett's Together
scenarios.note: Ideologically the closest fit, but Bennett and Lapid campaigned on replacing Netanyahu.

blockers.text: Bennett declared on election night that Netanyahu has lost.

מחל.stance: Netanyahu posted on Oct 30 that forming a government with the Arab-led parties is forbidden; Likud says the election was stolen.
red_lines: No government that depends on Arab parties

דרך.stance: After meeting Lapid on Oct 31, Eisenkot said any MK accepting his four principles could be a partner, and vowed to use a Knesset majority for a state inquiry, national service and repealing judicial-overhaul laws.
red_lines: Partners must accept his four principles

רק.stance: Lapid says Netanyahu has no way to form a government on these results, but forming an alternative will be complicated and is not guaranteed.

אמת.stance: On Nov 1 Golan said Netanyahu should not lead another Iran war and urged forming an alternative government quickly; he has backed including Arab parties since the election.

ל.stance: In a Facebook post on Oct 30, Liberman again ruled out a coalition with the Arab parties, saying he won't sit with supporters of terrorism; he also still won't sit with Netanyahu or the Haredi parties.

שס.stance: Unnamed Haredi sources say Deri has ruled out an opposition-led government without Likud and would join a unity government only alongside Likud.

ג.stance: Chairman Yaakov Asher consulted the party's rabbis on Oct 31, and Ynet reports UTJ wants exemption legislation before committing to either candidate.

ב.stance: Ben-Gvir held a long meeting with Netanyahu on Oct 29 on preserving a right-wing government, his party says; he rejects unity with Eisenkot.

ט.stance: Smotrich met Netanyahu in person on Oct 29, Ynet reports, and says the Arab party heads should be questioned by the Shin Bet over alleged foreign funding.

עם.stance: Abbas denies any link to the alleged foreign interference, pledges full cooperation with investigators and accuses Netanyahu of inciting against Arab citizens; he has said he'd join a government that tackles crime and discrimination.

ודם.stance: Tibi said on Oct 31 the Joint List is ready to recommend Eisenkot and replace the Knesset speaker but will not join the government, offering outside support.

Channel 12 reports he told party members that an Eisenkot minority government relying on outside Arab support would be weak or impossible.
Acting director Dean Livne tells Channel 12 he sees no likelihood the interference allegations will change the results, with individual votes voided only on direct proof.
